paper.title_en: The Relativistic Contraction-Shrinkage Theory (RKST): Emergent gravity from vacuum contraction and discrete scale invariance for the unification of cosmology.
paper.abstract_en:
The standard cosmological model is coming under increasing pressure due to accumulating observational anomalies. The discrepancy between local and global measurements of the Hubble constant (the Hubble tension), the fundamental Cosmological Constant Problem (CCP), the persistent lack of direct evidence for dark matter, and the unexpected maturity of early galaxies observed by JWST all point to an epistemological crisis. The Relativistic Contraction-Shrinkage Theory (RKST) presents a fundamental reinterpretation of these phenomena. By formulating a ghost-free scalar-tensor theory, it is shown that the gravitational constant G emerges from the coupling between a microscopic scale (the proton radius r_p) and the cosmological Dirac number N.

In this paper, we demonstrate that r_p is necessarily derived from the CCP discrepancy factor 10^123 and a discrete scale invariance. We show that the RKST resolves the Hubble tension as an environmental effect within the KBC void, provides a causal explanation for the JWST anomalies through dynamic gravitational amplification in the early universe, and reproduces the structure of the CMB as standing cosmic waves.
